source.title: Electromyography and Neuromuscular Disorders: Clinical-Electrophysiologic-Ultrasound Correlations

principles.rule: Treat localization as the primary organizing step of an EDX interpretation.
Interpret NCS and needle EMG in the context of symptoms, symptom duration, examination and differential diagnosis.
Classify neuropathic patterns by predominant motor, sensory or sensorimotor involvement.
Assess whether the overall electrodiagnostic pattern is primarily axonal, demyelinating or mixed.
Compare the electrodiagnostic pattern with the clinical time course and distinguish acute, subacute and chronic evolution where supported.
Evaluate spontaneous activity, MUAP morphology and recruitment as a combined pattern.
When neuromuscular transmission disease is suspected, consider repetitive stimulation and exercise testing in addition to routine NCS and needle EMG.
Use neuromuscular ultrasound as complementary structural and dynamic information alongside EDX physiology.
Before interpreting an abnormality, consider technical quality, temperature, stimulation, recording, artifacts and laboratory-specific reference ranges.
